subject: bat
pitch: A fruit bat with its wings spread wide. A fluffy golden-brown body, a fox-like face with big dark eyes and a moist black nose, pointed ears, and leathery charcoal wings stretched between long finger bones with a small hooked claw on each thumb. It clutches a half-eaten fig in its feet.
reasoning:
I want to keep things simple and safe given uncertain SDK details, sticking close to the reference API. I'm picturing a fruit bat hovering with wings spread, clutching a fig in its feet, positioning the fig's bottom at y=0 so the lowest point touches the ground plane.

Given uncertainty around exact joint and chain signatures, I'll minimize risk by relying mainly on b.part and b.joint, writing a helper function to build rods between two points by computing midpoint position and direction so geometry aligns properly along the bone axis.

For wings, rather than trust an unknown membrane API, I'll construct the surface manually with triangulated geometry, duplicating faces reversed so both sides render. I'm planning the skeleton hierarchy—body, chest, head, jaw, shoulders, elbows, wrists, fingers, hips—parented joint by joint, and sizing everything like a flying fox with roughly 1.5m wingspan and 0.3m body length, scaled up a bit for presence.

Now I'm working out body positioning: torso center around y=0.42, head/fig region near y=0.07 with small radius, hips around (±0.05, 0.38, -0.1) with legs extending down to feet near (±0.04, 0.13, 0).

Still placing body geometry...

Working out the head details next: skull and tapered snout shapes, a black nose with a tiny highlight, a separate lower jaw piece with its own pivot joint, and positioning for the dark eye spheres.

Now I'm figuring out the ears as outward-tilted cones with pink inner coloring, and devising a generic helper function to build directional cone/cylinder shapes between two points with varying radii, considering how to orient the geometry correctly along an arbitrary direction vector.

For the wings, I'm plotting out the joint coordinates for each side—shoulder, elbow, and wrist—to create a bat-like outstretched arm shape, estimating positions based on a scaled-up wingspan proportional to a fruit bat's anatomy.

Now I'm sketching the finger skeleton extending from the wrist: a small hooked thumb claw plus several longer fanning digits, each with a knuckle joint and tip, trying to keep the overall span realistic while simplifying the positions for each fingertip.

Still mapping wing membrane geometry...

For panel B, I'll order the fan from a centroid through S, E, W, K5, T5, A, B1 back to S, checking it stays star-shaped with a slight sag in y. I'll add a small propatagium triangle near the neck to cover the region in front of the arm, and keep weighting simple by rigging the whole membrane to a single shoulder bone for now.

For coloring, I'm using a charcoal base with darker finger bones and a subtle bluish tint on the membrane, alternating panel shades slightly for variation. Since the wing needs to be double-sided, I'm duplicating vertices for front and back faces rather than sharing them, since shared verts would cause computeVertexNormals to average to zero — mirroring the right wing to the left by flipping the X sign.

Now I'm placing the thumb from the wrist out to its tip with a small curved claw cone, then setting up the arm bones as tapered rods from shoulder to elbow to wrist, adding a bit of fur fluff near the shoulder, and chaining joints from wrist through knuckle to fingertip without bothering with a formal chain role, just named joints.

For the legs, I'm positioning hip, knee, and ankle joints with bat-like bends -- thigh angling down and back, shin angling forward -- then adding five little toe rods curving from the ankle over to grip the figure's surface near its center.

I'm settling on tiny claw cones at the toe tips and a simple ankle pad ellipsoid for the foot. For the fig, I'm planning a lathe-based teardrop body in purple-brown with a bitten section exposing pink-red interior, stem pointing up since the bat is clutching it from below.

Building the wedge cut-face geometry...

Now I'm defining the fig's profile curve for lathing, then placing toe contact points against that curved surface by computing the radial distance at a given height and solving for the matching z-offset so each toe sits flush on the fig's skin.

Working out the toe angles so they spread around the ankle with x positions ranging roughly 0.03-0.066 and wrapping away from the wedge front, then placing ankles near (±0.045, 0.17, -0.03) with the figure center around z=0.02 and body positioned above.

Now I'm lowering the body center to y=0.40 for a more compact pose, repositioning the chest ellipsoid and shoulders accordingly, and shifting the wing anchor points down by about 0.05 to match—starting with shoulder and elbow coordinates for one wing.

Continuing to place wing joint coordinates, checking that the wingspan (~1.6m) and drooping tip height stay realistic for a fruit bat, then shifting focus to the head: positioning the skull, snout, nose tip, eyes, and ear bases relative to the new body center.

Now I'm defining the jaw pivot and ellipsoid, plus a neck ruff ellipsoid in a lighter golden tone, and setting up the body's color palette with darker golden-brown fur, a lighter belly, and a lighter mantle collar. I'm also planning procedural fluff tufts as small cones scattered across the body surface using spherical parameterization with outward-facing normals for a textured furry look.

I'm now working out the skeleton structure—root body joint, chest, neck, head, jaw as a child of head, ears as children of head, and shoulder/hip joints for wings and legs, skipping a tail since this is a fruit bat. I'm also writing a helper function to generate tapered cylinder "bones" between joints for the rig visualization.

Now I'm adding an ellipsoid helper for rounder body parts and a membrane geometry helper for the wing surfaces, figuring out how the `at` positioning parameter places each mesh relative to its bone.

I'm detailing the facial features now: layered eye spheres with dark iris plus tiny white highlight dots, a small golden brow ridge, a moist black nose with a subtle highlight, thin whisker rods, and maybe tiny fang cones for a cute touch. Moving on to the ears, building a cone shape with golden outer fur and pink inner coloring.

Now I'm writing out the wing joint hierarchy with mirrored left/right coordinates, defining shoulder-elbow-wrist chains plus finger segments (knuckles and tips) for each digit, and planning the bar parts attached to each bone.

Setting up membrane panels on the rigid shoulder bone with alternating dark colors, plus foot joints (hip-knee-ankle) with toe bars and claws, and the thumb claw geometry with curved cone segments in a pale bone color.

For tufts, I'm placing random fur strands using spherical unit vectors scaled by radii, with normals pointing outward and tips extended along that normal, avoiding the front head region. Checking the figure's overall height bounds from feet at y=0 up through ears and wings, then finalizing joint naming and bone signatures before writing everything out.

Now I'm building the wedge geometry for lathe-style parts, constructing double-sided quads from profile points rotated around an axis, offset by the figure's center position, with the core ellipsoid placed and colored.

I'm adding flesh-colored inner faces and scattering small seed spheres near the wedge front, then checking that the lathe sweep angle and winding direction produce outward-facing normals correctly.
